current_example.title: Example: Finding the Rank or Nullity of a Matrix Given a Description of the Column or Null Space

q-141228.name: Question 1
q-141228.worked_solution:
According to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

For the given matrix, we have $n=8.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A) & =n \\ \text{rank}(A)+2 & =8 \\ \text{rank}(A) & =8-2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

q-141230.name: Question 6
q-141230.problem: Let $A$ be a $5\times 7$ matrix. If $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3},{b}_{4}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(A)$, find $\text{dim(Null}(A)).$
q-141230.worked_solution:
According to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

For the given matrix, we have $n=7,$ and since $B$ is formed by $4$ vectors, $\text{rank}(A)=4.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A) & =n \\ 4+\text{nullity}(A) & =7 \\ \text{nullity}(A) & =7-4 \\ \text{dim(Null}(A)) & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

q-141232.html:
Question 7
?

Let A be a 6×10 matrix. If B={b1,b2,b3,b4} is a basis of Col(A), find dim(Null(A)).

a
2
b
6
c
10
d
4
e
0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

According to the rank-nullity theorem, if A is a matrix with n columns, then

rank(A)+nullity(A)=n.

For the given matrix, we have n=10, and since B is formed by 4 vectors, rank(A)=4. Therefore,

rank(A)+nullity(A)=n4+nullity(A)=10nullity(A)=10−4dim(Null(A))=6.

q-142485.name: Question 8
q-142485.problem: Let $A$ be a $4\times 5$ matrix. If $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(A)$, find $\text{dim(Null}(A)).$
q-142485.worked_solution:
According to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

For the given matrix, we have $n=5,$ and since $B$ is formed by $2$ vectors, $\text{rank}(A)=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A) & =n \\ 2+\text{nullity}(A) & =5 \\ \text{nullity}(A) & =5-2 \\ \text{dim(Null}(A)) & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

q-139982.name: Question 9
q-139982.worked_solution:
According to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

For the given matrix, we have $n=4,$ since this is the number of components in each of the vectors of the null space. 

Also, since 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,|\,\,{x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R\}
$$

we conclude that $\text{nullity}(A)=3.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A) & =n \\ \text{rank}(A)+3 & =4 \\ \text{rank}(A) & =4-3 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
